title: Guardian papers, the $35 contract and the train to New York
summary: Buck's mother signs guardianship, each mother is promised $35 a week, and the boys go to New York with a manager named Irwin Rosen.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I go to Buck's mother and I get the guardian papers for Buck which she signs and everything and we get him out of school and I get my mother and all to get to the manager and everything and get the contract signed. They're going to pay my mother $35 a week and all expenses for me -- gonna give $35 a week to each mother. It was like a godsend to me, but not knowing what I know after getting to New

York. However, I take Buck's clothes and put them in my trunk so we'll only have one trunk with both sets of clothes. We go to to the railroad station to catch the train with roller skates. We catch the train and go to New York with the man and they got a man in New York to meet us -- I can't think of his name but the man that's going to manage us after we get to New York is Irwin Rosen, that's his name and he was in a band but nobody knew but him about it, I didn't know it. However, they don't get no bookings for us, they don't get no place for us to work. Finally got one job for us to work, first job we got after about almost a month there and we got a job in Staten Island at the St. George Theater in Staten Island -- was a good hit over there, good hit. Now only singing and playing piana and I'm singing out world this/-- you believe me, you believe me I'm singing. I could sing a while. However, we do that engagement, three days I think it was -- three or four days
